title: SRE mini-bridge: 21-day oncall readiness pack
body:
Purpose:
This is a compact, operational-first onboarding + hiring companion aimed at accelerating new or internal-transfer engineers to independent SRE oncall readiness in ~21 days. Focus: practical signal (can triage, fix common incidents, follow runbooks, escalate correctly), team fit, and low-friction access provisioning.

High-level goals (measured):
- Shadow-to-first-takeover: new hire takes first low-severity page by day 7, first medium by day 14, primary for low backfills by day 21.
- Access fidelity: 100% of required tool access by day 2.
- Competency gating: pass core interview rubric (see below) and peer sign-off at day 21.
- Ops hygiene: can create a postmortem draft and link to tuning tickets within 3 oncall shifts.

Audience and usage notes:
- People Ops uses this as the operational checklist for SRE hires and internal transfers.
- Hiring managers use the rubric during panel debriefs.
- New hires get this as a living doc at offer-accept + first-day packet.

21-day sprint (practical schedule):
Week 0 (prestart):
- Day -7 to -1: invite to #sre-new-hires and #sre-oncall, preboarding checklist sent, hardware request (if on prem) submitted, KMS onboarding ticket created.
- Provide: minimal reading bundle (runbook index, incident taxonomy, escalation matrix), intro video (10m), short org chart.

Week 1 (shadow + playbook basics):
- Day 1: orientation, tour of monitoring (Grafana), paging system (PagerDuty), Slack triage etiquette. Access validation (IAM, vault read-only, github, pagerduty).
- Day 2–3: Shadow low-severity pages with mentor. Walkthrough of a simple incident from page to postmortem.
- Day 4: Hands-on lab: restart a non-critical pod in staging (k8s cluster: redwood-staging), run basic kubectl debugging commands.
- Day 5: First solo low-severity takeover with mentor on-call present. Debrief + add notes to runbook.

Week 2 (expanding scope + ownership):
- Day 6–8: Triage medium-severity incidents under supervision, engage on-call rotation. Create at least one small remediation PR (e.g., alert threshold tweak).
- Day 9: Interview lab: pair with mentor to debug a simulated incident (recorded).
- Day 10: Cross-team rotation: join infra-support sync and product incident readout.
- Weekend: oncall shadow schedule (light pager duty) if rotation allows.

Week 3 (independence + evaluation):
- Day 11–13: Primary for several low/medium incidents; expected to escalate when appropriate. Draft postmortem on any substantive incident handled.
- Day 14–16: Operational tasks: access cleanup, entitlement review, sign-off on runbook edits.
- Day 17–21: Final evaluation window. New hire runs a mini-runbook improvement project (<= 4 hours) and presents results in retro. Final pass/fail decision by hiring manager + two peers.

Minimum access checklist (to verify day 1–2):
- [ ] GitHub org access (read + ability to open PRs)
- [ ] PagerDuty account, assigned to team schedule
- [ ] Slack: #sre-oncall, #platform-alerts, #dev-team channels
- [ ] AWS/GCP console read-only + assume-role for escalations
- [ ] Vault read-only + KMS test decrypt
- [ ] Monitoring (Grafana) and logs (Loki/ELK) dashboards access
- [ ] Runbook editor permission (Confluence / internal wiki)
- [ ] JIRA access to SRE board with create/edit tickets

Hiring plan + scorecard (role: SRE, IC3/IC4 depending on hire):
- Role narrative (short): Keep inference production systems healthy and low-latency; reduce MTTR; mentor cross-functional engineers on reliability.
- Core signals (what success looks like at 3 months): reliable oncall throughput, one postmortem contribution, two runbook improvements, at least one cost/efficiency ticket closed.
- Scorecard buckets (panel to score 1–5 each):
  - Troubleshooting fundamentals (syscalls, networking, k8s primitives)
  - Incident communication (clear, concise, escalation decisions)
  - Tooling fluency (monitoring, deployment, logging)
  - Ownership & follow-through (PRs, postmortems)
  - Cultural fit (collaborative, blameless, documentation-first)
  - Learning velocity (ramp history, ability to upskill quickly)

Interview rubric (practical, panel-friendly):
- Round 1: Take-home diagnostic (4–6 hour lab): triage a synthetic degraded pipeline (logs + metrics + playbook). Look for clear timeline, hypothesis-driven triage, minimal noisy changes.
- Round 2: Technical panel (60–75m): one debugging whiteboard problem (networking or resource constraint), one k8s scenario, one short behavioral/incident story.
- Round 3: Ops-sim panel (45m): live simulation with a mentor playing product PM; candidate makes triage and communications decisions.

Scoring guidance (example):
- 5 = Exceptional: accurate root cause hypotheses, executes safe remediation, updates runbooks, teaches others.
- 3 = Solid: correct triage, needed prompting for safe remediation, clear comms.
- 1 = Not ready: lacks repeatable triage flow or unsafe remediation choices.

Panel calibration quick-sheet (use during debrief):
- Did candidate form hypothesis fast? (Y/N)
- Did candidate consider blast radius before acting? (Y/N)
- Communication clarity: 1–5
- Post-incident hygiene: created tickets / runbook edits? (Y/N)

Sample behavioral prompts:
- Describe the last incident you handled end-to-end. What were the hardest decisions?
- Have you ever rolled back a production change? Walk us through your checklist.
- Tell us about a time you found and fixed a flaky alert. What was the root cause?

Onboarding deliverables (expected by day 21):
- Completed access audit (screenshot or ticket links)
- Two runbook edits or a single consolidated improvement and link to PR
- A draft postmortem of any incident they led or co-led
- 21-day retro notes and a 90-day personal learning plan

Mentor and evaluator guidance:
- Mentors must be on the same rotation weeks 1–3. Weekly 1:1s at day 7 and day 21 mandatory.
- Evaluators: hiring manager + two peers (one senior SRE, one cross-functional engineer). Evaluation form uses scorecard above and a pass/fail recommendation.

Risk and mitigation: known friction points
- Delayed access: escalate to IT with priority tag and use temporary shadow sessions until IAM completes.
- Pager overload: schedule lighter rotation for new hire first weekend; pair with mentor.
- Vendor credentials (HSM/KMS): pre-submit and require 48h lead time before start.

Notes to self / open items (work-in-progress):
- Consider a short recorded simulation (10m) we can reuse for the take-home diagnostic to reduce interview variance.
- Should we require a container basics checklist as prerequisite? (k8s fundamentals or a 2-hour self-study).
- Add a small rubric item for cost-awareness (e.g., flagged runaway jobs) — currently not explicit.

Appendix: quick links and templates
- New-hire ticket template: JIRA:SRE-NEWHIRE-TEMPLATE (create copy on start)
- Postmortem template: https://confluence.redwood-inference.local/sre/postmortem-template
- Runbook index: https://confluence.redwood-inference.local/sre/runbooks/index
- Slack channels: #sre-oncall, #platform-alerts, #infra-rotations

Versioning / ownership:
- Doc owner: Maya Desai (eng-sre). Please tag @maya for any edits.
- Status: draft — please push edits to the linked ops-playbooks repo and add PR link in linked_artifacts.

End of pack.

(Inline: this doc intentionally mixes operational checklists + hiring rubric so recruiters and hiring managers can share a single artifact during first 21 days).
